caption: Financial Terrorism
audio_content_summary: A single-thesis explainer: every U.S. war of the last 50 years can be read through the dollar. Traces the chain from Nixon ending gold convertibility (1971) and the 1974 U.S.-Saudi petrodollar arrangement, through the dollar's reserve status and Treasury-financed military spending, to the IMF/World Bank (1944) and structural-adjustment conditionality, to SWIFT cutoffs and a 2025 Lancet estimate of ~564,000 deaths/year from sanctions. Then a regime-change pattern for states that exit the dollar: Iraq (euro switch 2000 → invasion 2003), Libya (Gaddafi gold-dinar email, 2011), Venezuela (Maduro captured Jan 2026), Iran, Sankara's Burkina Faso (1987), and Cuba (1960 Mallory memo, 64-year embargo). Closes on de-dollarization: BRICS, gold-buying, the dollar's falling reserve share.
implied_frame: Frames the dollar as a coercive system and presents each intervention as punishment for leaving it. Verifiable, primary-sourced threads were turned into records (petrodollar 1974, World Bank-American-president convention, Iraq's 2000 euro switch, the 1960 Mallory memo, Sankara 1987, the 2011 Blumenthal/Libya gold email, the 2025 Lancet sanctions study). The causal claim that de-dollarization *is* the motive for each war is the reel's interpretation, not asserted by the records. Group B/C left out of records: specific structural-adjustment statistics (Latin American wages −40%, Colombia −84%, “305,000 excess infant deaths in Kenya alone”) could not be tied to a primary source; the Maduro capture (Jan 3, 2026) is real but its stated cause is the reel's framing; Cuba's claimed last-week fuel exhaustion with 22-hour blackouts is recent and unverified; the “British vote worth 41 times” IMF-quota figure was not pinned to a primary.
